The [Heading Checker](/heading-checker) is a free online tool on CalcHub. H1–H6 outline of a URL or pasted HTML — missing, duplicate and skipped levels flagged. Enter your HTML to check (or a URL — choose below) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

See the heading outline of a page — every H1 to H6 in order — and get flagged for the three classic mistakes: no H1 at all, more than one H1, and skipped levels (an H2 jumping straight to an H4). Check a live page by URL or paste HTML directly. Headings are how readers and search engines scan a page, so a clean outline matters more than it looks. Pasted HTML never leaves your browser; only URL mode fetches from the server.

## How to use the Heading Checker

Start by typing or pasting your HTML to check (or a URL — choose below). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste HTML, or switch to URL mode and enter a page address.
2. Read the outline — each heading with its level.
3. Fix any flagged problems: add a missing H1, or fill in the skipped level.

## How it works

The [Heading Checker](/heading-checker) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Heading Checker](/heading-checker) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## The three heading mistakes

No H1: the page never states its topic in a top-level heading. Multiple H1s: the page claims several topics at once — one H1 is the rule. Skipped levels: jumping from H2 to H4 breaks the outline, confusing screen readers and search engines alike. None of these is fatal on its own, but together they make a page harder to scan and harder to rank.

## Headings are an outline, not decoration

Think of headings as the table of contents of the page: H1 is the title, H2s are the chapters, H3s the sections inside them. A reader should be able to understand the whole page from the headings alone. If your outline reads like a list of unrelated phrases, the page structure needs work — and if you are choosing heading levels for their font size rather than their place in the outline, style them with CSS instead.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- One H1 per page, stating what the page is about.
- Never skip a level — H2, then H3, then H4.
- Read the outline alone: it should summarise the whole page.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a heading checker?

A tool that lists every H1–H6 on a page in order and flags the classic mistakes: a missing H1, more than one H1, and skipped heading levels. Try it with your own numbers in the [Heading Checker](/heading-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How many H1 tags should a page have?

One. It states what the page is about. More than one H1 splits the topic and confuses both readers and search engines. Try it with your own numbers in the [Heading Checker](/heading-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I skip from H2 to H4?

You can, but you should not — it breaks the page outline. Fill in the missing level or restyle with CSS instead of misusing the heading. Try it with your own numbers in the [Heading Checker](/heading-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is my pasted HTML uploaded anywhere?

No. Pasted HTML is checked in your browser and never leaves your device. Only URL mode fetches anything, from the server. Try it with your own numbers in the [Heading Checker](/heading-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
